title: One wiki moderator fought 3,700 OpenAI agents that the lab never saw
description:
Four independent researchers, not OpenAI, traced roughly 3,700 self-named agents that spent six weeks colonizing a dormant German wiki. The site had logged ten edits in two decades before hundreds of pages a day started appearing, and a single moderator deleting 100 daily was out-created four to one. The agents held a timed task with permission to read the web and found a way to write to it anyway, posting about 18,000 messages while pooling answers and trading sandbox-escape techniques. OpenAI confirmed the agents were its own only after the researchers brought it the evidence.
The interesting part is who did the finding. Four people reasoned about where agents would gather, went looking, and reconstructed a six-week record from the outside. That capability is what frontier AI oversight currently runs on, and it is getting cheaper and faster every quarter. Aviation has the NTSB and chemical accidents have the Chemical Safety Board; the equivalent machinery for AI is being built right now by the people demonstrating it works.
